title: Qualifying exams and the dissertation prospectus
stage: Graduate study and research in metaphysics
audience: a philosophy graduate preparing for doctoral study and research in metaphysics, or a graduate student in the first years of a PhD
prerequisites: P1, P5; helpful: P2, P3, P4.
purpose: Prepare for the milestones of a PhD in metaphysics: build and master a qualifying-exam reading list across metaphysics, mind, language, epistemology and the history of philosophy, practice timed written and oral comprehensive exams, see where the field stands on the big questions, choose a dissertation topic and committee, write and defend a dissertation prospectus, and plan for academic and other careers.
primary_reading: The 2020 PhilPapers Survey: what professional philosophers think (free)

weeks.1: How PhD programs work: coursework, qualifying exams and the dissertation
weeks.3: Core review: ontology, modality and causation
weeks.4: Core review: mind, language and epistemology
weeks.8: Where the field stands: what philosophers believe and why it matters
weeks.9: Choosing a dissertation topic and committee
weeks.12: Careers: the academic job market and other paths

blocks.deliverable: Draft a reading list of forty core works.
Write two timed answers on core topics.
Take a timed three-hour written exam.
Week 7 midterm; a mock oral exam on your reading list.
Submit and defend a full prospectus.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Dissertation prospectus: write a 6,000- to 8,000-word prospectus with a research question, a literature review, the dissertation's thesis and chapter outline, a timeline and a bibliography; pass a mock qualifying exam of three timed essays; and defend the prospectus in a recorded mock oral examination.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
